items.headline: Thursday sell-off: S&P 500 down 2%, Nasdaq down 2.3%, Dow down 2.2% as AI doubts spread
items.note: The S&P 500 closed at 7,175.83 (-147.80 points), the Nasdaq at 23,879.20 and the Dow at 49,097.06 (-1,101.11 points), as investors grew less sure the AI boom keeps driving growth. This is the latest close I could confirm; I couldn't find Friday's.

items.headline: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq: opens at $111.50, closes at $97.17
items.note: ANT priced at $83 and ended its first day up 17.1% after opening about 34% higher, per CNBC via Forbes Australia. Volume topped 600 million shares by early afternoon. A big AI listing landed on the same day AI stocks fell.

items.headline: Anthropic staff can sell up to 10% of shares on day one; another 35% frees up early next year
items.note: Per Business Insider reporting summarized in search results, not confirmed on the original page. It's an example of a lock-up schedule, which matters if you ever get equity at a company that goes public.

items.headline: Nvidia under pressure: Huang out as CEO, Treasury's Bessent demands an outside successor
items.note: Jensen Huang resigned Nov. 12 and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Bessent gave the board 10 days to answer questions about China-related chip sales, and Commerce Secretary Lutnick will testify to the Senate Banking Committee Dec. 10. Export-control and governance news now moves AI chip stocks.

items.headline: Nvidia fell 2.9% after earnings despite $115.8B in revenue
items.note: Revenue was up 103% from a year earlier with a ~$130B forecast, yet the stock slipped on the CEO transition and doubts about how long AI spending lasts. A good report no longer guarantees a rising stock.

items.headline: Fed minutes: nearly all officials expect a December rate hike
items.note: Minutes from the Oct. 27–28 meeting show nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December, with two floating a half-point. Higher rates tend to pressure tech and growth stocks.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.note: Reported to improve professional work, coding and computer use at lower compute cost; Astra's input price is 20% below the original model's. I only saw summaries, so check OpenAI's page for specifics.

items.headline: Tech layoffs top 142,000 this year, but data science skills hold up better
items.note: Layoffs.fyi counted 142,000+ tech layoffs at 350 companies as of Nov. 11. Data and analytics roles look more resilient than general tech postings, though entry-level hiring in AI-exposed jobs is weaker, so internship competition is likely tough.

learn.explain: A drawdown is how far an investment has fallen from its most recent peak, usually shown as a percentage. If a fund goes from $100 to $90, it's in a 10% drawdown, and it needs an 11% gain to get back to $100. Thursday's 2% one-day drop in the S&P 500 is a small drawdown on its own, but drawdowns add up across days: the index also had a multi-day losing streak this week. Looking at the maximum drawdown shows how painful holding something could have been, not just its average return.
learn.try: Search for the S&P 500's maximum drawdown in 2022 and compare it with its drop this week.
